decisions.decision: The choices are ScrapTypeCatalog.All followed by the arrangement's own types, composed by one ScrapTypeCatalog.Compose rule that the arrangement editor also calls.
decisions.why: FR-002 forbids a second scrap-type list, and the ordering and de-duplication rule existed only as a private static in the Settings editor, so a second caller would have duplicated it.
decisions.rejected: A scrap-type table with its own stored procedure, or a third private copy of the ordering rule in the generic flow.

decisions.decision: LuggerArrangementSnapshot gains WasRead, set true by Create and false by Empty.
decisions.why: The service returns Empty both for a failed read and for an arrangement with no rows, so no caller could tell an outage from an empty arrangement, which FR-010 and the spec's edge case both require.
decisions.rejected: Making GetSnapshotAsync throw, which would leave GetLuggersAsync beside it still swallowing, or adding a second throwing read to the same interface.

decisions.decision: GenericRequestScrapOption loses AvailableLuggerCount and AvailableLuggerDisplay, and the page loses its two count columns and the GenericRequest_Scrap_Luggers label.
decisions.why: Nothing populates the count, because the read behind it has always been the stub, so it is a leftover of the Temp preview that FR-014 deletes. Every lugger fact in the spec belongs to the card, and a count taken at load would be stale by the time a handler read the card.
decisions.rejected: Populating the count from the snapshot the step already reads, which puts a non-spec'd number on a 30-second screen and tells a different story from a card that deliberately draws a blocked lugger with its status.

decisions.decision: The stated type is recorded as GenericRequestScrapAnswer under the key scrap.type in the existing answers_json column.
decisions.why: It is the column the generic flow already uses for a per-answer record, and storing the requester's wording is what makes FR-011 and FR-013 hold when the arrangement changes.
decisions.rejected: Writing the type into input_value, which is documented as the one value the request is about and would give the same fact two authorities, or adding a column and its schema artifacts.

decisions.decision: The lugger is resolved by one routine in RequestJobAvailabilityProvider, reached by the existing work-order path and by a new GetStatedScrapLuggerAsync for a stated type.
decisions.why: FR-007 and SC-003 require the two card kinds to name the identical lugger in every case, and only one routine guarantees that. The provider already holds the arrangement and picture services.
decisions.rejected: Resolving in WaitlistViewViewModel, which would duplicate the picture lookup, or storing the lugger on the request, which assumption A2 forbids.

decisions.decision: The board merges the stated type and resolved lugger into the RequestJobPartAvailability it already passes to CreateSessionOrder and ResolveDeclaredCell.
decisions.why: It is the record that already carries ScrapType, LuggerLocation and LuggerLocationImagePath to the two places that draw them, so no title, cell rule or template needs a second branch and the work-order card is untouched.
decisions.rejected: Reading the answer inside WaitlistRequestTitles.ResolveContext, which would fix the type token only and leave the lugger arriving by a second mechanism.

decisions.decision: The scrap step injects the existing ILuggerArrangementService instead of introducing a reader seam in MTM_Waitlist.Shared.
decisions.why: 018 needed a seam because the implementation belonged to Setup; here the contract is in Core, which has no project references and is already referenced by GenericRequest, so a new interface would be an interface with one implementation for nothing.
decisions.rejected: An IScrapTypesReader in Shared mirroring IDunnageCatalogueReader.

decisions.decision: The scrap step gates Continue on a chosen type and re-selects the draft value with a trim and OrdinalIgnoreCase comparison.
decisions.why: CanAnswer is true in the base class, so FR-004 is currently unimplemented and the forward button is enabled with nothing chosen; the stored draft can differ from the option only in case or surrounding spaces, which the arrangement already treats as one type.
decisions.rejected: Leaving the gate inherited and relying on CommitToDraft to keep the previous value.

decisions.decision: Promoted the composition rule into ScrapTypeCatalog.Compose and made the editor call it, trimming each name before the case-insensitive compare
decisions.why: The editor's private copy compared untrimmed, so "5052 ALUMINUM " would have been offered beside "5052 aluminum"; one home also stops the step and the editor drifting on order
decisions.rejected: Leaving the editor's private copy and writing a second composition rule in the generic step

decisions.decision: StatedScrapLugger carries ArrangementRead rather than letting the caller read Rows.Count
decisions.why: An outage and an arrangement with no rows were indistinguishable before WasRead existed, and the card has to word them differently
decisions.rejected: Having the caller test Rows.Count, which cannot tell the two apart

decisions.decision: The board merges the stated scrap facts into a per-request copy of the availability after ResolveJobAvailabilityAsync
decisions.why: The merge is per request while the cache is per work centre, and CreateSessionOrder and ResolveDeclaredCell stay byte-identical for the work-order path
decisions.rejected: Merging inside CreateSessionOrder, which the work-order path and the existing card tests also call

decisions.decision: The configuration-gap warning keys off WasRead instead of Rows.Count > 0
decisions.why: WasRead is the exact question the old proxy was approximating; an arrangement that was read and holds no rows is a real configuration gap worth recording
decisions.rejected: Keeping Rows.Count > 0, which also stays silent for a genuinely empty arrangement

decisions.decision: The gap and outage card phrases are proven by resolving the key and by the resw declaring it, not by asserting the value differs from its key
decisions.why: The test host has no resource index, so GetLocalized returns the key there; asserting inequality fails for a reason unrelated to the feature
decisions.rejected: Asserting the value differs from its key, which cannot pass in this test host

decisions.decision: The stated scrap type is asserted on the card's identifier line (Subtitle) rather than Title
decisions.why: pickup-scrap's line 1 is its category word and its line-2 template is {scrap_type}, so the identifier is where the stated type actually lands
decisions.rejected: Asserting on Title, which carries the category prefix and fails

approach: The scrap step reads the compiled ScrapTypeCatalog plus the live lugger arrangement and offers their union, gating Continue on a chosen type.
